scope: Samba 4.23.10 native Kerberos, Java21, BC, Direct TCP; 16/32-byte GSS keys, owned/borrowed callers and signing/GCM; all eight existing public profiles extended with peer GSS denial and fresh-session recovery.
behavior: A one-byte alteration to a genuine initial GSS token is applied before SMB signing. The peer returns a signed STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE; the existing channel key authenticates the error before any retirement effects. This is not an expired-server-ticket or invalid-SMB-signature test.

After verified peer denial, the SDK fences the old logical Session, closes pending and established owned channels, releases leases and async ownership, and publishes the existing identity-scoped logoff event. It does not send target LOGOFF to the deleted remote session.

New I/O on the old open fails locally within the two-second test bound. The old Session cannot reauthenticate or publish new channels. Borrowed caller transports and older unrelated sessions remain usable; a fresh Session and open complete real I/O.

Local GSS/cache failures, local authenticator SMBApiException failures, unsigned errors and tampered signatures do not invoke this retirement path. The accepted peer status remains primary when retirement cleanup throws IOException or Error.
Established SessionContext key bytes and preauthentication value are retained rather than replaced; original-key reservations are never reset. Fresh-session recovery is separately authenticated.

focused_check.note: Before adding the two cleanup-failure parameter variants; those are included in the full local check.

audit_scope: Independent JCE primitives verify observed tags and actual-key/nonce identities per profile. Keys are exported from the client; the observer does not independently derive GSS keys from wire authentication tokens. Bounded traces are not a lifetime-wide proof.
regression_boundary: Four native signing-only cases at e145831 passed the signed STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE checks, then timed out writing the revoked handle. Earlier principal-substitution, masked-cleanup, interrupted and compilation attempts are retained separately as unqualified diagnostics. Only 18 recorded readiness container IDs were present in those retained reports, and each was confirmed absent.
provenance: CUSTOM peer-denial retirement and focused/native coverage on the approved current baseline. The existing nested-session logoff loop is extracted unchanged for reuse during local retirement. No third-party implementation or dependency was imported.
